scope: Independent source-only review of renderedAnalysisPeople WeakMap and canonical member opener. No new browser execution or app edits; parent save/outcome test evidence remains separate.

checks.assessment: onDataChange derives a first-name-match map and full person-ID navigation list from the currently loaded analysis before setting analysis=null. It records stable IDs only for existing rendered data-analysis-person buttons.
Map inserts a name only once, preserving former Array.find first matching name behavior. Same-name ambiguity is neither newly resolved nor worsened by this presentation cache.

Actual delegated button is passed to openAnalysisPersonModal; captured mapping takes precedence, otherwise live analysis lookup is retained. Canonical workspace arguments preserve selected ID, current isAdminUser(), existing callback, full navigation IDs and duties tab. No API path/payload changed.

The captured array is a fresh analysis.people.map result shared across captured buttons. Member workspace reads ids/indexOf and indexes for previous/next; no mutation of the provided array found. It is not Object.freeze immutable, but current consumers treat it as read-only.

WeakMap keys are DOM buttons. Route/session DOM removal makes entries eligible for collection; resetPrivateSessionView aborts view listeners and removes private surfaces. No localStorage, public DOM identity injection or permission changes introduced.

When analysis is already null, later invalidations leave prior button snapshots intact, preserving still-rendered links. A fresh rendered button has no inherited mapping and uses current analysis fallback. This matches intended existing rendered snapshot behavior.
No scheduling, allocation, calculation, persisted data, export content or backend source changes appear in this fix.

bounded_followup_checks: Parent actual canonical-save regression should prove an existing rendered analytics member link still opens exact prior ID after cache invalidation, including profile next/previous context.
A same-name fixture should retain first-match selection if explicit identity ambiguity coverage is needed; current source proof is not runtime test evidence.

If future code reuses the same button node for a different person without replacing it, snapshot invalidation must accompany that reuse. Current inspected analytics renderers replace markup rather than mutate person identity on existing buttons.
